document:
Spring IoC container and dependency injection
Spring manages application objects as beans in an IoC container. Study bean definitions, dependency relationships, scopes and lifecycle before learning framework-specific annotations. Distinguish object creation managed by the container from objects created directly by application code. Ask which component owns a dependency and how that affects testing.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/core/beans.html

document:
Spring MVC and the Servlet stack
Spring MVC is the Servlet-based web framework in Spring Framework. It is distinct from the reactive WebFlux stack. Start with HTTP request and response semantics, mappings, binding, conversion, validation and errors. Choose examples for the intended stack rather than mixing reactive and Servlet assumptions.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc.html

document:
DispatcherServlet request processing
DispatcherServlet is the front controller for Spring MVC. It delegates request mapping, handling, view resolution and exception handling to configured components. Trace the request through these collaborators to diagnose routing failures. Spring Boot can initialize an embedded container through its own startup sequence.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc/mvc-servlet.html

document:
Controller mappings inputs and responses
Annotated MVC controllers express request mappings, input handling and exception handling through annotations. Their methods need not inherit a controller base class. A controller returning a view name differs from one producing a response body. Establish the intended HTTP contract before choosing annotations or return types.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/web/webmvc/mvc-controller.html

This starter is a reading roadmap; it does not contain a compiled application or certify dependency compatibility.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/index.html

document:
Auto configuration and explicit configuration
Spring Boot attempts to configure an application based on available dependencies and configuration conditions. Auto-configuration does not remove the need to understand the resulting beans. Inspect configuration decisions before adding manual configuration. Study how application-provided beans can replace default behavior and why changes to dependencies can change the application context.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/using/auto-configuration.html

document:
Externalized properties and environment configuration
Spring Boot supports configuration from property files, YAML, environment variables and command-line arguments. Property-source precedence matters when values differ between environments. Separate deploy-time configuration from code, and test which value the application resolves. Use the version-specific reference when learning binding and configuration precedence.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/features/external-config.html

document:
MockMvc request testing
MockMvc exercises Spring MVC request handling using mock requests and responses without starting an HTTP server. It is useful for checking mapping and response behavior, but it does not replace every end-to-end network test. Choose a test scope that matches the failure you want to observe.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/testing/mockmvc.html

document:
Spring Boot testing plan
Plan application tests at more than one scope. Distinguish focused component tests from tests using a broader application context. The Boot testing reference documents supported test utilities. Before adding executable exercises, pin dependencies and define expected HTTP responses, validation failures and integration behavior.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/testing/index.html

document:
Transaction boundaries and data access
Spring provides transaction management abstractions and declarative and programmatic approaches. Model the business operation and its failure boundaries before choosing transaction annotations. Exercises should verify rollback behavior and consistency, not merely annotation presence. Check the exact release documentation when teaching transaction propagation and proxy-related behavior.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/data-access/transaction.html

document:
Spring Security for Servlet applications
Keep security lessons specific to the Servlet stack when using Spring MVC. Separate authentication from authorization and test allowed and denied requests. Use the official Spring Security reference for configuration APIs in the chosen version. This reference card is not a verified security configuration or a production security assessment.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/index.html

Spring Data JPA learning scope
Spring Data JPA documentation is a source for repository-oriented persistence lessons. A future pathway should connect entity modeling, repository queries, pagination and transaction boundaries with actual database tests. Keep JPA persistence topics separate from general Java collection exercises and do not label an unexecuted persistence example as verified.
Source: https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/jpa.html
